send /files itself to the API, so a download is not the web app's index.html

The local disk signs its links as /files?key=...&signature=..., whose path is /files itself. The @api matcher listed /files/* only, so Caddy sent those requests to the web app's catch-all, which answers index.html with 200 text/html: an issued PDF, an export or an attachment was saved as a file of the right name and the wrong content ("the generated PDF is corrupted"). Only stacks that run caddy/Caddyfile with STORAGE_DRIVER=local showed it: pnpm dev proxies /files by prefix, S3 links point at the bucket, the Helm Ingress matches by prefix, and the Caddy test asked for /files/a.

- caddy/Caddyfile: /files in the matcher, next to /files/*.
- caddy/caddyfile.test.mjs: asks for the link as the disk issues it (GET and PUT), and for paths that merely start with "files".
- documents e2e, pwa-paths and dev-proxy tests: the link's shape and path are pinned.
- the matcher as it is, what mirrors it, restarting Caddy after a Caddyfile-only change, and a pitfall.

expose exchangeRates in GET /v1/features

The features answer says whether the deployment fetches exchange rates (EXCHANGE_RATES_FETCH), so the web app can hide money pages where there are none. Typed client regenerated, changeset added, docs/configuration.md updated. Closes.

offer MFA enrolment while the features are unknown; lead to setup on mfa_enrollment_required

The MFA section shows "unavailable" only when the features are known and mfa is off; while they load or fail it offers enrolment. When me.mfaEnrollmentRequired is set it starts enrolment straight away. A 403 mfa_enrollment_required from any query shows one notice and sends the user to the MFA setup page. Closes.

tamper the sealed secret's tag deterministically

Replacing the tag's last two characters with AA left it unchanged when it already ended that way, or differed only in base64's unused bits, so the test failed now and then. It now changes the tag's first character.

keep GET /v1/features open during MFA enrolment; refuse requireMfa for an unenrolled caller

GET /v1/features is marked @DuringMfaEnrollment, so a user who must still enrol can see the switches and the enrol UI. Turning auth.requireMfa on at a scope that covers the caller, while they have no authenticator, is refused with 409 mfa_enroll_first, so an administrator can't lock themselves out. Closes.

leave mail transports and lock-decorated jobs out of Observe's instrumentation

Observe runs methods with its proxy as `this`, which breaks @nestjs/mail's downleveled private fields and @nestjs/locks' instance-keyed job runners. skipInstrumentation now skips every @nestjs/mail *Transport and any class with a method @nestjs/locks wrapped (found by its marker, so new jobs are covered). use all CPUs for the web tests on CI

CI's web job runs this package's Vitest alone, so maxWorkers is 100% there (121 s instead of 186 s on 4 CPUs); local runs keep 50%. docs/pitfalls.md notes why CI's PostgreSQL keeps max_connections=100 (service containers take no command) and why the API's unit tests stay isolated. Closes

Main's longest job ran the whole unit and e2e suites in two shards (~6 min). Six shards like e2e's, each with a sixth of e2e and a third of the API's or the web app's unit tests, so main's run is as short as a pull request's. Closes

skip runs for labels other than destructive-migration

Every label event started a run in the same concurrency group as the push's, which it then cancelled. A run for any label but destructive-migration now gets its own group and a skipped job. Closes

cut a pull request's run from ~10 min to ~3 min

The run is as long as its longest job: template-without-notes ran the full unit and e2e suites behind lint and build (9 min), the e2e shards took 4.5 min each and check ran the unit tests after build. A pull request's run is ~3 min (was ~9.5).

deactivate the account when SCIM deprovisions its last membership

When the IdP's deprovisioning (DELETE, or active false) leaves an account
no active membership in any tenant, the account is deactivated in the same
transaction (users.deprovisioned_at), every session and token family ends,
and scim.account-deactivated is audited. Nothing is deleted. Provisioning
it again, active true, or an administrator re-enabling a membership brings
back the same account; a deleted account never comes back.

enterprise SSO (SAML 2.0, OIDC) and SCIM 2.0 provisioning, part 1

Tenants can add SAML (@node-saml/node-saml) or OIDC (openid-client) connections, off by default and managed under /v1/sso/connections with Access.manageSso. SAML accepts only signed assertions bound to a browser-started request, with audience, expiry, issuer and replay checks; OIDC uses PKCE, state and nonce and requires a verified email. Sign-in and provisioning only accept DNS-verified domains, looked up on the sso queue through an SSRF-guarded fetch. SCIM 2.0 Users and Groups at /v1/scim authenticate with a hashed API-client key holding Access.provisionScim. OIDC client secrets are stored encrypted.

encrypted columns, blind indexes and re-encryption (roadmap 5, part 1)

An EncryptionService (AES-256-GCM, HKDF-derived keys, HMAC-SHA-256 blind indexes) and a column registry: encrypted(), encryptedText(), blindIndexText(). Stored values are v1.<key id>.<iv>.<ct>.<tag>, bound by their AAD to the table, column and tenant. Keys come from DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEYS and BLIND_INDEX_KEYS (newest first, environment or _FILE only), and boot is refused when a declared column has no keys. An hourly scheduler queues per-tenant re-encryption jobs that rewrite rows still on an older key with compare-and-set writes, and the workers expose encrypted_rows_on_old_key.

a tenant tree for holding groups with consolidated reads

Tenants get a parent_id and a tenant_closure table kept in the same transaction as the tenant write; cycles, the operator tenant and parents pending deletion are refused. Every tenant table's read policy now only admits app.tenant_id or its descendants in the tree, so a child never reads its parent or siblings. Consolidated reads of a subtree are opt-in behind Access.readConsolidated, run read only, and are audited in the reader's tenant and every tenant read.

an AI helper module (roadmap 15)

A provider-agnostic AI module with an Anthropic adapter, off unless ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set and the tenant opts in (ai.enabled). Features register an AiSource that only exposes fields the requester may read. Summarize and classify tasks run on the ai queue with pinned prompt versions and Zod-validated structured output. Includes a per-tenant daily token cap, a Redis cache, audit entries, realtime ready/failed events, and the data export and account deletion hooks. Prompts and outputs are not stored in PostgreSQL.

Patterns print the record's own fields ({region}, one counter per value),
variables (FY, ABBR, and ones features declare) and the date parts JJJ and
WW. A series may take its dates from a date field of the record, and
conditions with a priority pick the series for a record (Frappe's Document
Naming Rule). The preview is POST /naming-series/preview with sample values.

targeting rules for feature flags

Flags take an ordered list of rules at the tenant and platform scopes. Each rule has conditions from a closed catalog (principal kind, role, verified email domain, locale, tenant slug, operator tenant) and an outcome of on, off or a rollout percentage. The first match wins before that scope's plain value, and conditions that can't be evaluated fail closed. Rules are validated and audited on write, and the web app has a rules editor in the flag dialog and the platform section.

harden passkeys against cross-origin ceremonies

Passkey assertions with crossOrigin set or a topOrigin are refused after the challenge is consumed, renaming a passkey needs recent authentication, and the sign-in log records tenant refusals on both the passkey and /v1/auth/token routes.

assertTenantWall now recreates each declared policy on a pg_temp copy inside a rolled-back savepoint and compares command, roles, USING and WITH CHECK with the live policy, so an edited policy expression no longer passes the check.

Postmark and SendGrid bounce and complaint intake

Sending already supported Postmark and SendGrid; their bounces and complaints now reach the suppression list too. POST /v1/webhooks/mail/postmark checks a shared secret (POSTMARK_WEBHOOK_SECRET); POST /v1/webhooks/mail/sendgrid verifies the signed Event Webhook (SENDGRID_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_KEY) and refuses stale timestamps. SES stays the default.

Closes

a deactivated tenant exposes nothing to account exports or queued client jobs

The account export read each tenant by membership alone, so a member of a deactivated tenant exported its records; it now yields only the membership row there. stillActive() also required only the API client to be active; it now requires its tenant active too, as API key sign-in does.

Closes

platform-wide feature flags, kill switches and rollouts; @RequireFlag(); useFlag()

Operators set a setting for every tenant (PUT/DELETE /v1/settings/{key}/platform): a runtime default below each tenant's values, an enforced value above them all (a kill switch), or a flag's rollout across every tenant. @RequireFlag(FLAG) answers 404 while the flag is off for the caller. The web app gets useFlag(key) and an "All tenants" section on /settings.

Administrators define naming series per numbered subject, written as Frappe

default; a record's create body may name another (namingSeriesId). A series
restarts when its date parts change, and its counter can be started at a value,
never below what is taken.

The privacy page test waited in real time for an export expiring 1.2 s after render, which failed under CI load. It now fakes only Date, catches the expiry timer as it is set, moves the clock past it and fires it: no real waiting.

declare a domain event once for webhooks, notifications and realtime

request queues a job; a worker fills an autoescaping template (@nestjs/mail's

completes the job adds the PDF to the record as a locked attachment.

email deliverability: SES bounces and complaints, a suppression list (22)

Amazon SES publishes bounces and complaints to an SNS topic, which POSTs
them to POST /v1/webhooks/mail/ses. The intake (a MailEventIntake, so
Postmark, SendGrid… are adapters of their own later) checks the format
and a Timestamp of the last hour, that the signing certificate URL is
https on an sns.<region>.amazonaws.com host at
/SimpleNotificationService-<id>.pem (nothing else is ever fetched; the
certificate must be small and valid now), that the topic is in
SES_SNS_TOPIC_ARNS, and the RSA signature (versions 1 and 2, version 2
alone with SES_SNS_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE_V2), then confirms a subscription or
queues the events; nothing is written in the request. A queue job, as
system:mail-intake, records each event once (unique per message and
recipient: replays are no-ops) and keeps the suppression list: hard
bounces and complaints suppress at once, soft bounces at
MAIL_SOFT_BOUNCE_THRESHOLD within MAIL_SOFT_BOUNCE_WINDOW_HOURS and for
MAIL_SOFT_BOUNCE_SUPPRESSION_HOURS only (a delivery resets them), a
stronger reason replaces a weaker one; audited.
